**Tier 2** — canonical — the only tier humans edit · owned by `data-ingestion` · `public.multi_tier_supply_chain`

**One row is** One directed firm-to-firm relationship in a project's multi-tier network: who supplies whom, at what depth, and in what capacity. An EDGE between two firm identifiers — not a party, and not a material flow: nothing here says what moves along it or how much.

DESCRIBED IN PHASE 3 / WP 3.2, AND THE DESCRIPTION IS MOSTLY A LIST OF ABSENCES. The deferral that pointed here called these "the other inbound datasets, each with its own bespoke upload path". `tier2_suppliers` and `tier3_suppliers` are that; this table is not. NO APPLICATION PATH PUTS A ROW IN IT: `UploadWizard` offers no template, no screen and no edge function writes it, and no CSV names a column of it — which is why every `ingest.csv_header` above is null. THE DATABASE HAS A WRITE PATH ANYWAY, and the third correction WP 6.2 made is this one. `bulk_insert_multi_tier_supply_chain` exists, it is already on `dataPlaneAudit.test.ts`'s list of tier-2 writers, and it works — `rehearsal/240` §6c calls it and reads the row back. What is true is that NOTHING CALLS IT: no file in `src/` or `supabase/functions/` names it, which is why the reader below is answered with an empty array on every real project. But an RPC with no caller is not an absent write path. This application runs as `anon` against permissive grants (D28), so anyone holding a PostgREST client is one call away from writing this table — the same sentence WP 4.1 wrote about the three legacy `ingest-*` functions before `ingest_legacy_upsert_lane` turned their target list into a whitelist in a migration. The claim is APPLICATION-level; the grant surface is WP 7.1's. AND "NO READER AND NO WRITER" WAS FALSE IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, WHICH THIS FILE HAD ALREADY RECORDED AND ITS OWN PROSE DENIED. The `surfaces` block above lists THREE confirmed entries, and WP 6.2 verified all of them against a real database: · `get_project_datasets` SELECTs this table and returns its rows, and   `projectLanes.ts` calls it from `/policies` and `/simulation-lab` — so it HAS a   live reader, feeding two pages. · `delete_project_dataset` has a `multi_tier` branch AND deletes from this table   in its `'all'` branch, which is what the "Delete ALL data" button on the project   manager invokes — so it has a live path that EMPTIES it. Two statements of one fact, in ONE FILE, disagreeing, with nothing comparing them: §4 D101's shape one scope tighter, and the generated page renders the PROSE half, so the contradiction was published to users. `supabase/rehearsal/240` §6 inserts a row, reads it back through the reader and watches the button's RPC remove it. `contract:check` R15 now refuses a note that denies a surface the same file confirms. What is true, stated once: nothing WRITES it, two pages READ it, and one button CLEARS it. Every occurrence is in migrations — created 2025-08-20, carried through RLS rewrites since, most recently by `20260915000004`'s organization dual read, which rewrote policies governing access to a table nobody can reach. EVERY `ingest.csv_header` ABOVE IS NULL FOR THAT REASON: there is no CSV to name a column of. It is described here rather than deferred again because a deferral is a promise that someone will look, and five packages of looking have now established what there is to see. DROPPING IT WAS NOT WP 3.2'S CALL — a table is not removed by the package that happened to notice. Its gap check added the count to §15 so that the package which does decide is deciding against a number, AND THE NUMBER IS ZERO: run `35143830532`, 2026-09-16, reports 0 rows across 0 projects, and run `35399391429`, 2026-09-19, agrees. WP 6.2 IS THE DECIDING PACKAGE AND ITS DECISION IS TO KEEP THE TABLE. The number says the benefit of dropping it is removing an empty relation. The cost, measured: rewriting `delete_project_dataset` — a live RPC behind a user-facing button — rewriting both dataset-snapshot builders, bumping `hash_network`'s `schema_version` 3 -> 4, which invalidates every stored network digest, deleting a published manual page and its registry entry, and updating four test files and a rehearsal — AND, found by the gate above, rewriting `get_project_datasets`, which two pages call on every load. That is a large and IRREVERSIBLE production change whose only gain is tidiness, taken against a row count measured days earlier. The table contributes an empty array to every project's `hash_network` today and costs nothing measurable. THE DECISION RESTS ON THE CORRECTED FACTS AND NOT THE ROW'S. §4 D58 argued from "no reader and no writer", and had the drop been taken on that premise it would have broken a reader two pages use. The number was right and the sentence beside it was not, which is the whole reason a decision waits for a measurement. What WAS wrong is the published claim, and that is corrected above rather than left standing: a page telling users nothing touches this table, while a button does, is the same defect as D103.

Two policies through the project's organization, the same pair `tier2_suppliers` carries: `org_is_current_user_org(p.organization_id, p.organization)` for SELECT, and the same predicate plus modeler-or-admin for writes. `audited: true` SINCE WP 3.2. No trigger existed before it, because WP 2.3 instrumented the tables the contract DESCRIBED and this was not one of them — the qualifier in `dataPlaneAudit.test.ts` is exactly the hole, and writing this sidecar is what made it visible. `20260916000016` adds the three triggers. On a table nothing writes they will never fire, which is the point: the rule is about every tier-2 table, not about the ones that happen to be busy.
